function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

**Park Ji‑sung** (박지성) – often written in Western order as **Ji Sung Park** – is a retired South‑Korean professional footballer who is widely regarded as one of the most successful Korean players in European football history.

| Category | Details |
|----------|---------|
| **Full name** | Park Ji‑sung (박지성) |
| **Date of birth** | 25 March 1981 |
| **Place of birth** | Seoul, South Korea |
| **Position** | Midfielder (primarily a box‑to‑box central midfielder) |
| **Height** | 1.78 m (5 ft 10 in) |

### Club Career Highlights

| Years | Club | Appearances | Goals |
|-------|------|-------------|-------|
| 1999–2000 | Suwon Samsung Bluewings (K League) | 30 | 4 |
| 2000–2001 | PSV Eindhoven (Eredivisie) | 55 | 7 |
| 2001–2004 | Manchester United (Premier League) | 71 | 4 |
| 2004–2005 | PSV Eindhoven (loan) | 32 | 3 |
| 2005–2008 | PSV Eindhoven | 86 | 6 |
| 2008–2011 | PSV Eindhoven | 73 | 4 |
| 2011–2013 | PSV Eindhoven | 54 | 3 |
| 2013–2014 | PSV Eindhoven | 28 | 1 |
| 2014–2015 | PSV Eindhoven | 27 | 1 |
| 2015–2016 | PSV Eindhoven | 20 | 0 |
| 2016–2017 | PSV Eindhoven | 12 | 0 |
| 2017–2018 | PSV Eindhoven | 12 | 0 |
| 2018–2019 | PSV Eindhoven | 12 | 0 |
| 2019–2020 | PSV Eindhoven | 12 | 0 |
| 2020–2021 | PSV Eindhoven | 12 | 0 |
| 2021–2022 | PSV Eindhoven | 12 | 0 |
| 2022–2023 | PSV Eindhoven | 12 | 0 |
| 2023–2024 | PSV Eindhoven | 12 | 0 |

> *Note: The table above condenses his long tenure at PSV, where he made over 400 appearances in all competitions.*

### International Career

- **South Korea U‑20** – 1999 FIFA U‑20 World Cup (gold medal)
- **South Korea Senior Team** – 2000–2018
  - **Caps**: 108
  - **Goals**: 12
  - **Major tournaments**: 2002 FIFA World Cup (Runners‑up), 2004, 2008, 2012, 2014, 2018 FIFA World Cups, 2006, 2010, 2014, 2018 AFC Asian Cups.

### Major Achievements

| Competition | Years | Result |
|-------------|-------|--------|
| **Premier League** | 2002–03, 2006–07 | Champions (Manchester United) |
| **FA Cup** | 2003–04 | Winners (Manchester United) |
| **UEFA Champions League** | 2007–08 | Winners (Manchester United) |
| **UEFA Cup** | 2004–05 | Winners (PSV Eindhoven) |
| **Eredivisie** | 2004–05, 2005–06, 2006–07, 2007–08, 2008–09, 2009–10, 2010–11, 2011–12, 2012–13, 2013–14, 2014–15, 2015–16, 2016–17, 2017–18, 2018–19, 2019–20, 2020–21, 2021–22, 2022–23, 2023–24 | 20 titles (PSV Eindhoven) |
| **FIFA World Cup** | 2002 | Runners‑up (South Korea) |
| **AFC Asian Cup** | 2004, 2010, 2014, 2018 | 4th place (2004), 3rd place (2010), 4th place (2014), 4th place (2018) |
| **Olympic Games** | 2004 | Bronze medal (Athens) |

### Playing Style & Reputation

- Known for his **endurance**, **work rate**, and **versatility**—capable of playing both defensive and attacking midfield roles.
- Nicknamed “The Korean Messi” early in his career for his dribbling and vision.
- Praised for his **tactical intelligence**, **passing accuracy**, and **stamina**; often described as a “box‑to‑box” midfielder who could contribute defensively and offensively.
- One of the first Korean players to become a regular starter in the English Premier League, paving the way for future Korean stars.

### Post‑Retirement

- **Coaching**: After retiring in 2024, Park joined PSV’s coaching staff as a **midfield coach** and later became an **assistant manager** for the club’s senior team.
- **Media & Commentary**: He has appeared as a football analyst on South Korean sports networks and occasionally provides commentary for international matches.
- **Philanthropy**: Active in various charitable initiatives, including youth football development programs in South Korea and the Netherlands.

### Other Notable Ji Sung Park(s)

If you were referring to a different individual named Ji Sung Park (e.g., a scientist, artist, or public figure), please let me know, and I can provide information on that person instead.

---

**Quick Takeaway:**  
Park Ji‑sung (Ji Sung Park) is a celebrated former South Korean midfielder who enjoyed a highly successful club career in the Netherlands and England, earned over 100 caps for his country, and remains a respected figure in football both on and off the pitch.
